resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and German source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, route checks, and generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded German pass identified 25 remaining circuit, TCR, thermal, SI-unit, and wire-gauge wording issues; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent German human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The resistance example title used an imperative phrase rather than a concise noun phrase.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Finden Sie Widerstand’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Widerstand bestimmen’.

findings.summary: The voltage example title used an inconsistent imperative form.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Finden Sie Spannung’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Spannung bestimmen’.

findings.summary: The heating explanation used Wärmefluss where the page consistently discusses heat-flux density.
evidence: The previous paragraph described Wärmefluss without the density qualifier and used a literal surface-loss construction.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with Wärmestromdichte and clearer energy-transfer wording.

findings.summary: The constant-resistance relationship used an unnecessarily literal production phrase.
evidence: The previous bullet said doubling current ‘produziert’ four times the heat effect.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the direct relation ‘vervierfacht sich die Wärmeleistung’.

findings.summary: The constant-current relationship repeated the doubling phrase awkwardly.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘verdoppelt eine Verdoppelung’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘verdoppelt sich ... wenn sich der Widerstand verdoppelt’.

findings.summary: The constant-voltage TCR paragraph used compressed syntax for resistance and current changes.
evidence: The previous paragraph joined the positive-TCR condition and current tendency without a clear clause structure.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with explicit constant-voltage and constant-current relationships.

findings.summary: The TCR limitation paragraph used a literal first-order estimate phrase.
evidence: The previous paragraph ended with ‘erste Ordnung Schätzung’.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with clear German for a first-order approximation and its real-world deviations.

findings.summary: The waveform-variable bullet omitted natural German articles and repeated und.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘A ist Amplitude ... t die Zeit ...’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘A ist die Amplitude, f die Frequenz ... t die Zeit ...’.

findings.summary: The angular-frequency unit used an inconsistent Bogenmaß construction.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘im Bogenmaß pro Sekunde’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the standard wording ‘in Radiant pro Sekunde’.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating setup used a compressed compound around the energy example.
evidence: The previous setup used a less natural ‘41,8-kJ-Beispiel’ construction.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a direct instruction to heat the 41,8-kJ example from a constant 100-W source without losses.

findings.summary: The area-conversion instruction omitted the definite article.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘Konvertieren Sie Fläche’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Wandeln Sie die Fläche in m² um’.

findings.summary: The heat-flux definition did not consistently distinguish heat-flux density from heat capacity.
evidence: The previous paragraph used Wärmefluss while the title and formulas used Wärmestromdichte.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with consistent Wärmestromdichte terminology and a clear surface-crossing explanation.

findings.summary: The length-conversion setup used an unnecessary repeated imperative.
evidence: The previous setup used ‘Konvertieren Sie ... in ...’ with an awkward second unit phrase.
findings.resolution: Changed it to natural German for converting 0,1 Zoll to millimetres and 5 mm to inches.

findings.summary: The imperial-dimension note used English unit names.
evidence: The previous paragraph ended with ‘Zoll, Quadratzoll und Kubikzoll’ in a mixed construction and used a literal relation phrase.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with consistent German for mass, force, and the three imperial dimensions.

findings.summary: The unit-check title used the less natural Gerätekontrollen.
evidence: The previous title was ‘Praktische Gerätekontrollen’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Praktische Einheitenprüfungen’.

findings.summary: The unit-check bullet used an untranslated English imperative.
evidence: The previous bullet said ‘Convert before multiplying or dividing’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘Wandeln Sie die Einheiten vor dem Multiplizieren oder Dividieren um’.

findings.summary: The rounding instruction used an incomplete imperative and less natural precision phrase.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘Rund nur zu letzt’ style wording.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a complete instruction to round only at the end.

findings.summary: The AWG expansion used an imprecise translated system name.
evidence: The previous bullet called AWG ‘amerikanische Drahtstärke’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘AWG steht für American Wire Gauge’ and retained the historical Brown-&-Sharpe name.

findings.summary: The SWG description omitted the standard system name and used a compressed compound.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘Draht- und Blechdickensystem’ without a clear system-name expansion.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with the standard name and clear German description.

findings.summary: The BWG description used a literal past-tense construction.
evidence: The previous bullet said the system ‘wurde früher ... verwendet’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to concise German describing its historical use for iron wire, pipes, and sheet thickness.

findings.summary: The system-identification instruction used the vague verb nennen.
evidence: The previous bullet began ‘Nennen Sie das System’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise specification instruction ‘Geben Sie das System an’.

findings.summary: The nominal-diameter instruction used a compressed ‘Systeme verwechselt’ phrase.
evidence: The previous bullet did not clearly state when systems may be confused.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with ‘wenn Systeme verwechselt werden können’.

findings.summary: The conductor-dimension instruction used an incomplete material noun phrase.
evidence: The previous bullet did not clearly distinguish a blank conductor from the isolated diameter.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with clear German for blank conductor, insulation, sheet thickness, and pipe-wall thickness.

findings.summary: The stranded-conductor instruction used a literal term for wire construction.
evidence: The previous bullet used ‘Litzenkonstruktion’ without a direct specification verb.
findings.resolution: Changed it to a direct instruction to specify the Drahtkonstruktion when flexibility and total diameter matter.

findings.summary: The resistance explanation used Materialwiderstand rather than the standard material property term.
evidence: The previous paragraph referred to ‘Materialwiderstand ρ’.
findings.resolution: Changed it to ‘spezifischer Widerstand ρ’ and clarified the three-size AWG relationship.
